findings.evidence: Eligibility para 3: 'In addition, eligibility for the workspace stipend depends on several details the reviewer checks one at a time...The reviewer confirms the workspace address...The reviewer logs every workspace confirmation...' Program Coordination: 'The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout. The team logs each request the moment it arrives.' Review Responsibility: 'The determination of stipend eligibility happens before any payment goes out. The escalation of repeat requests happens automatically within the same quarter.'
findings.fix: Either separate employee-facing instructions from administrative process descriptions into distinct sections with clear headings indicating the audience, or remove administrative-only sections and replace them with information the employee actually needs.
findings.location: Eligibility section paragraph 3, and sections 11-12 (Program Coordination, Review Responsibility)
findings.violation: The document addresses multiple audiences - employees, managers, reviewers, and administrators - within the same sections without clearly separating them. The Eligibility section paragraph 3 discusses workspace confirmation from the reviewer's perspective ('the reviewer checks', 'the reviewer confirms', 'the reviewer logs'), mixing reviewer procedures with employee eligibility criteria in the same paragraph. Sections 11-12 (Program Coordination, Review Responsibility) describe internal administrative processes entirely from a non-employee perspective, without signaling that this content is not directed at the reader applying for the stipend.

findings.evidence: 71-word sentence, 5 subordinate-clause markers: Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device because fieldwork regularly takes the employee away from the single fixed desk that the standard equipment list assumes every applicant has for the whole benefit year while the finance office tracks the second device against the same annual amount that the equipment catalog publishes for each category.
findings.fix: Split the sentence at a subordinate-clause boundary.
findings.violation: The sentence runs to 71 words with 5 subordinate-clause markers, longer than the reader can hold in mind on a single pass.

findings.evidence: 71-word sentence: Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device because fieldwork regularly takes the employee away from the single fixed desk that the standard equipment list assumes every applicant has for the whole benefit year while the finance office tracks the second device against the same annual amount that the equipment catalog publishes for each category.
findings.fix: Move subordinate clauses and modifiers after the main clause, not between its subject and verb.
findings.violation: At 71 words, with 0 comma-set-off clause(s) and 5 subordinate-clause marker(s), the sentence stacks interruptions between its subject and its main verb instead of holding the main clause together.

findings.evidence: Title: 'Home-Office Equipment Stipend Policy'. Eligibility para 3: 'eligibility for the workspace stipend depends on...'. How to Apply para 1: 'Employees must submit the receipt, the manager's approval form, and the original purchase order'. Required Documentation para 1: 'Employees keep proof of purchase for every stipend item. A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests.' Restrictions para 1: 'The applicant must keep the equipment in good working condition'. Restrictions para 2: 'the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device'.
findings.fix: Add a definitions section or opening paragraph clarifying: (1) the distinction or equivalence between 'equipment stipend' and 'workspace stipend'; (2) that 'the applicant' and 'the employee' refer to the same person; (3) the exact documentation submission requirements (is 'proof of purchase' equivalent to 'receipt' or 'purchase order', or are they different items?).
findings.violation: Multiple terms are used interchangeably for the same concept without signaling that they mean the same thing, forcing readers to verify whether terms refer to the same document or concept: (1) 'equipment stipend' appears in the title and Program Overview, while 'workspace stipend' appears in Eligibility, with their relationship never clarified; (2) 'the applicant' in Restrictions and Exceptions paragraphs 1-2 and 'the employee' throughout Eligibility, Required Documentation, and Reimbursement Amounts are used for the same person without definition; (3) The submission requirement 'the receipt, the manager's approval form, and the original purchase order' (How to Apply para 1) vs. 'proof of purchase' (Required Documentation para 1) vs. 'A photo of the receipt' (Required Documentation para 1) creates ambiguity about what documents must be submitted vs. kept, and which proof format is acceptable.

findings.evidence: Employees must submit the receipt, the manager's approval form, and the original purchase order before the review begins.
findings.fix: Reformat the inline items as a numbered or bulleted list.
findings.violation: The sentence embeds three or more comma- or semicolon-separated parallel items inline rather than presenting them as a formatted list.

findings.evidence: Additionally, employees shall retain receipts for one year after the purchase date.
findings.violation: The sentence states a binding requirement using shall or an indirect requirement phrasing instead of must.

findings.evidence: The finance office conducts an evaluation of every submitted receipt before it approves the amount.
findings.fix: Restate the nominalized noun as the sentence's main verb.
findings.violation: The action is buried inside the noun 'evaluation', carried by a generic support verb, instead of stated as the sentence's own main verb.

findings.evidence: Section sequence: 1-Program Overview, 2-Eligibility, 3-How to Apply, 4-Approval Timeline, 5-Required Documentation, 6-Reimbursement Amounts, 7-Restrictions and Exceptions, 8-Terminology Notes, 9-Request Steps, 10-Special Cases, 11-Program Coordination (internal process), 12-Review Responsibility (internal process), 13-Questions and Updates. The 'Request Steps' section should appear at position 3 or 4, not position 9.
findings.fix: Reorder sections to follow the reader's task sequence: Eligibility → Request Steps → How to Apply → Required Documentation → Approval Timeline → Restrictions. Move administrative-process sections (Program Coordination, Review Responsibility) to an appendix or remove them if they don't serve the reader's task.
findings.violation: The document does not follow the reader's actual task sequence. The 'Request Steps' section appears as section 9, after 'Terminology Notes' and before 'Special Cases', and well after sections describing internal administrative processes ('Program Coordination' at section 11, 'Review Responsibility' at section 12). A reader applying for a stipend needs 'Request Steps' much earlier - immediately after 'Eligibility' - so they understand what they need to do before diving into administrative details. The inclusion of sections describing internal processes that don't help the reader complete their task further breaks the logical task flow.
